Day 70 of 100 · Docker

Multi-Container Deployment

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityDockerPublished artifact recovered

The Docker capstone connected image build, private networking, persistent storage, health checks, secrets and runtime hardening into one small application system.

Architecture / mental model

client → 127.0.0.1:8080 → app → backend network → PostgreSQL → db-data volume
                                           ↘ secret file

How it works

The published stack built the application locally, ran PostgreSQL from a pinned image, used a named volume for database data and delivered the database password through a Compose secret file instead of a plain environment value.

The application host port was bound to loopback, reducing unintended external exposure, while the database lived only on the backend network.

Database health was part of application startup semantics. Compose then became the capstone artifact connecting concepts from images, containers, networks, volumes, Dockerfiles and container security.

Hands-on reference

docker compose config
docker compose up -d --build
docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f
docker compose down

Verification

Make a real request to the application, verify database persistence after service recreation, inspect network membership and confirm the secret value is not committed in the Compose file or printed into logs.

Field note / gotcha

`depends_on` can control startup ordering, but 'started' is not 'ready.' A health condition is required when the application must wait for the database to become usable.

Security considerations

Keep the database unpublished, bind external-facing ports intentionally, use non-root/read-only/capability controls where the workload permits and manage production secrets with a suitable secret system.

What I learned

The phase is complete when storage, communication, startup and privilege are deliberate parts of one system rather than isolated Docker commands.
